vulnerability.title: Symfony Request::create accepts browser-sanitized URIs, enabling open redirects through validators built on it
vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: annotated tag v5.4.45 peels to 2b66d7d7..., whose Request.php blob matches the fix commit's parent e39f6a96; the fix is absent from this tag

severity.source: NVD primary metric nvd@nist.gov; the GitHub_M CNA and GHSA use a different 3.1 LOW vector
severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD primary CVSS 3.1 numeric 6.1 falls in Medium (4.0-6.9); the CNA/GHSA vector scores 3.1 LOW and is recorded as a source disagreement

entry_point.description: Public static factory used by applications and by validators that derive a Request from a user-supplied URL string. The URI argument is the attacker-controlled value in the open-redirect scenario.

critical_operation.description: In 5.4.45 create() delegates URI parsing to PHP parse_url and never validates the input against the WHATWG URL rules that browsers apply. parse_url accepts backslashes, CR/LF/TAB, NUL bytes, and leading/trailing spaces or control characters, and it resolves them differently from a browser. A validator that calls Request::create on a user-supplied redirect target can therefore extract a host that differs from the host the browser will navigate to, which is the open redirect. Fixed releases insert four guards after parse_url: reject a false parse result, reject a backslash before the query/fragment delimiter, reject CR/LF/TAB anywhere, and reject a leading or trailing byte <= 0x20; invalid input raises BadRequestException.

trace.description: entry: application passes an attacker-influenced URI string to Request::create
parse_url is the only parsing step; there is no invalid-character assertion in 5.4.45
the parsed host is copied into SERVER_NAME/HTTP_HOST, so callers see the parse_url host rather than the browser host

source_crosscheck.notes: NVD scores the issue 6.1 MEDIUM with AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N. The CNA record (GitHub_M), the GHSA page and OSV all carry 3.1 LOW with AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N. NVD's vector changes the scope to CHANGED and adds low integrity impact; that is NVD's own enrichment, not the reporter's. The canonical severity keeps the NVD Primary 6.1 and records the 3.1 LOW as a source disagreement. All four families agree on CWE-601, on the mechanism, and on the three fixed releases. OSV's version arrays are internally inconsistent in spelling (some entries '2.0.4', later entries 'v2.0.10') but the range events are consistent with the advisory. The independent reviewer additionally found that OSV's affected.versions list omits several released tags inside its own ranges (v5.4.41, v5.4.43, v6.4.1, v6.4.5, v6.4.6, v6.4.9, v6.4.11, v7.1.2, v7.1.4), and that GHSA/OSV carry a CVSS v4.0 2.3 vector absent from the CNA and NVD records. The reviewer's own canonical severity uses the CNA 3.1 LOW vector; this dossier keeps NVD Primary 6.1 MEDIUM and records both.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No browser, HTTP client or PHP runtime was executed. The mismatch between PHP parse_url and WHATWG browser parsing is taken from the advisory and the upstream regression test, not measured locally.

The exploitation step is application-specific: the advisory describes a validator that calls Request::create on user input and redirects to the resulting URL. No concrete downstream application is part of this repository snapshot, so the redirect sink is outside the mapped location.
The vulnerable snapshot is v5.4.45, the last 5.4 release before the fix; the 6.4 and 7.1 branches were checked only for fix ancestry and fixed-file content, not inventaried.
The GitHub REST advisory endpoint was rate-limited from the shared egress IP; the advisory page was read as HTML instead and the failed response was not treated as evidence.
The repository snapshot has 11040 tracked files and 150 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.
No dynamic red/green test was run, so no reproduction_reference exists and the entry is grade B at best.

OSV's range events are correct, but its affected.versions enumeration omits released tags inside those ranges: v5.4.41, v5.4.43, v6.4.1, v6.4.5, v6.4.6, v6.4.9, v6.4.11, v7.1.2 and v7.1.4 were confirmed to exist upstream by the independent reviewer. Scanners keyed to the list rather than the range under-report.

The CNA record and NVD carry no CVSS v4.0 entry, while the GHSA page and OSV add CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N (2.3 LOW). Only the v3.1 vectors are used for the canonical severity.
NVD keys the product as CPE vendor sensiolabs:symfony; the CNA, GHSA and OSV key the Packagist package symfony/http-foundation. The monorepo tags are the same source.
The upstream credit differs: the Symfony blog names only Sam Mush, while GHSA/OSV add IPASSLab and ZGC Lab. This does not affect the technical fields.
The fix commit's author date is 2024-10-22 and its committer date is 2024-10-29; ancestry, not date, is used for the release boundaries.
open_questions: Which concrete browser/parse_url input pair the reporters used is not published; the regression test lists the rejected classes but not an end-to-end redirect.
Whether applications commonly pass raw user input to Request::create as a redirect validator was not surveyed.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Request::create at v5.4.45 and confirm the absence of invalid-character validation around parse_url.
An independent reviewer must confirm 5a9b08e is absent from v5.4.45/v6.4.13/v7.1.6 and an ancestor of v5.4.46/v6.4.14/v7.1.7.
An independent reviewer must check the severity split between NVD 6.1 and CNA/GHSA 3.1 and the single CWE-601 claim.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
